title: 开漏输出：3.3 V 单片机送出 5 V 高电平
summary: 一个耐 5 V 的 FT 引脚设成开漏输出，外接 4.7 kΩ 上拉到 5V。起始电路用的是不耐 5 V 的 PA0。测开漏低、开漏高和推挽高三种情况。
description: R1（4.7 kΩ）从开发板 5V 脚接到信号结点 OUT5，OUT5 接一个设成开漏输出的引脚。开漏输出只能把线拉到 GND，“高”的时候松手，由上拉电阻把线拉到 5 V——所以这个引脚必须耐 5 V。起始电路里 OUT5 接在 PA0（不耐 5 V）上。

cards.title: PA0 想送出 5 V
text: 起始电路：**`4.7 kΩ`** 的电阻 R1 从开发板 **5V** 脚接到信号线 OUT5，OUT5 接在 **PA0** 上。
单击开发板，看引脚表：PA0 设成了**「输出 高」**，并勾选了**「开漏」**。
看右边的**「诊断」**：OUT5 到了 5 V 吗？想一想上一个实验里，藏在普通引脚里的那只二极管。

cards.title: 开漏：只会拉低，不会推高
text: - 普通的**推挽**输出里有两个开关：上面一个接 3.3 V，下面一个接 GND。**开漏**输出拆掉了上面那个，只剩一个通往 GND 的开关。
![](fig:od)
- **输出低**：开关合上，OUT5 接地，电流从上拉电阻灌进引脚。**输出高**：开关断开，引脚“松手”，上拉电阻把线拉到它接的电压——这里是 5 V。
- 输出低时灌进引脚的电流，就是上拉电阻上的电流：
- 代入整 5 V：$I = \frac{5}{4700} ≈ 0.0011$ A，引脚轻松吃得下。
- 松手时引脚上真的是 5 V，所以它必须**耐 5 V**。PA0 不行：它的保护二极管把线钳在 3V3 上面一点点。要用 FT 引脚。

cards.title: 换到 FT 引脚
text: - 把 OUT5 的信号线从 PA0 挪到一个 **FT 引脚**（下排，例如 **PB12**）。
- 在引脚表里把它设成**「输出 高」**，勾选**「开漏」**。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**。通过后，按测量题依次换成开漏低、开漏高、推挽高，量 OUT5 的电压和 R1 的电流。
- 先预测：推挽输出高时，上拉电阻里的电流往哪边流？

cards.title: 带走
text: - **开漏输出只会拉低**；“高”由上拉电阻决定，上拉到几伏就是几伏。所以它能做电平转换，前提是引脚耐得住那个电压。
- 上拉电阻常用 **1–10 kΩ**：越小边沿越快，但输出低时灌电流越大。
- **I²C 就是开漏总线**：几个芯片可以共用一根线而不打架。Blue Pill 的 I²C 引脚是 FT，可以上拉到 5 V。
- 真实电路里的坑：ESP32 没有耐 5 V 的引脚，开漏上拉到 5 V 同样会倒灌。要用 BSS138 一类的电平转换模块。FT 引脚接 5 V 上拉时，也**不要**再打开内部上拉。

caption.text: 开漏引脚 = 一个通往 GND 的开关 S。合上：OUT5 被拉低，电流 I 从上拉 R1 灌进引脚。断开：R1 把 OUT5 拉到 5V。

i18n.en: An open-drain pin = a switch S to GND. Closed: OUT5 is pulled low and the current I flows from the pull-up R1 into the pin. Open: R1 pulls OUT5 up to 5V.

en.startNote: **Fix-it**: the 5 V pull-up R1 is wired, but the signal goes to the non-5 V-tolerant **PA0**. **Why**: open-drain with a 5 V pull-up needs a 5 V-tolerant (FT) pin. **Your job**: move the signal wire to the FT pin PB12 (h1) and set PB12 to open-drain output.
en.title: Open drain: a 3.3 V chip sending a 5 V HIGH
en.summary: A 5 V-tolerant FT pin set to open-drain output, with an external 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 5V. The starting circuit uses PA0, which is not 5 V-tolerant. Measure open-drain LOW, open-drain HIGH and push-pull HIGH.
en.description: R1 (4.7 kΩ) runs from the board's 5V pin to the signal node OUT5, and OUT5 goes to a pin set to open-drain output. An open-drain output can only pull the line to GND; for "HIGH" it lets go and the pull-up takes the line to 5 V — so the pin must be 5 V-tolerant. In the starting circuit OUT5 is on PA0 (not 5 V-tolerant).

cards.title: PA0 tries to send 5 V
text: Starting circuit: a **`4.7 kΩ`** resistor R1 from the board's **5V** pin to the signal line OUT5, and OUT5 on **PA0**.
Click the board and look at the pin table: PA0 is set to **output HIGH** with **open drain** ticked.
Look at the **diagnostics** on the right: does OUT5 reach 5 V? Think of the diode hidden inside an ordinary pin in the previous experiment.

cards.title: Open drain: it pulls down, it never pushes up
text: - An ordinary **push-pull** output has two switches: the upper one to 3.3 V, the lower one to GND. An **open-drain** output removes the upper one, leaving only a switch to GND.
![](fig:od)

- **Output LOW**: the switch closes, OUT5 goes to ground, and current flows from the pull-up into the pin. **Output HIGH**: the switch opens, the pin "lets go", and the pull-up takes the line to whatever it is tied to — 5 V here.
- The current the pin sinks when LOW is the current in the pull-up:
- With a round 5 V: $I = \frac{5}{4700} ≈ 0.0011$ A — easy for a pin.
- When it lets go there really are 5 V on the pin, so the pin must be **5 V-tolerant**. PA0 is not: its protection diode clamps the line a little above 3V3. Use an FT pin.

cards.title: Move to an FT pin
text: - Move OUT5's signal wire from PA0 to an **FT pin** (bottom row, for example **PB12**).
- In the pin table set it to **output HIGH** and tick **open drain**.
- Press **Check my circuit**. Once it passes, switch to open-drain LOW, open-drain HIGH and push-pull HIGH as the questions say, and measure OUT5's voltage and R1's current.
- Predict first: with a push-pull HIGH, which way does the current in the pull-up flow?

cards.title: Take away
text: - **An open-drain output only pulls down**; HIGH is whatever the pull-up is tied to. That makes it a level shifter — as long as the pin can stand that voltage.
- Pull-ups are usually **1–10 kΩ**: smaller gives faster edges but more sink current when LOW.
- **I²C is an open-drain bus**: several chips share one line without fighting. The Blue Pill's I²C pins are FT and may be pulled up to 5 V.

- A real-world catch: the ESP32 has no 5 V-tolerant pins, so an open-drain pull-up to 5 V leaks back into it too; use a level-shifter module such as a BSS138 board. On an FT pin with a 5 V pull-up, **don't** also turn on the internal pull-up.

compare: - Open-drain LOW: V = **0.04 V**, sinking **0.99 mA** (= 4.69 V / 4.7 kΩ).
- Open-drain HIGH: V = **4.69 V** (the 5V pin), zero pin current.
- Push-pull HIGH: only **3.31 V**, and **0.29 mA** flows back from 5 V through the pull-up into the pin. With VIH ≈ **3.5 V**, a 5 V CMOS input may not count 3.3 V as HIGH.

**Why it must be an FT pin**: at open-drain "high" the pin sees 5 V. A normal pin has a clamp diode to 3V3 that holds OUT5 at about 3.9 V (3.3 V + one diode drop), with current flowing from 5 V through the pull-up and the diode into 3V3 — it can't output 5 V and it back-feeds the supply. An FT pin has no such diode and withstands 5 V.

measurements.explain: The N-channel switch is about 40 Ω: 40 Ω × 0.99 mA ≈ 40 mV.

measurements.ask: Open-drain LOW: the current in the pull-up R1 (the current the pin sinks)
measurements.explain: 4.69 V / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.99 mA. A smaller pull-up gives faster edges but more sink current in LOW.

measurements.ask: Open-drain HIGH (pin released): OUT5 to GND
measurements.explain: The pin lets go, R1 carries no current, and OUT5 equals the 5V pin's 4.69 V — an FT pin has no clamp diode to 3V3, so nothing holds it down.

measurements.ask: Push-pull HIGH instead: OUT5 to GND
measurements.explain: The high-side switch holds OUT5 at about 3.3 V, below a 5 V CMOS input's VIH ≈ 3.5 V: it may not count as HIGH.

measurements.ask: Same state: the current in R1 (from the 5V pin toward the pin)
measurements.explain: (4.69 − 3.31) / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.29 mA flows back from 5 V into the pin and on into 3V3: push-pull is fighting the 5 V pull-up.

hints: Starting circuit: PA0 is not 5 V-tolerant. Move the signal wire to an FT pin on the bottom row, for example PB12.
Only one resistor: 4.7 kΩ from the 5V pin to the signal node.
In the pin table choose output HIGH and tick open drain.
tests: Open-drain LOW: close to 0 V, sinking the pull-up current
Open-drain HIGH: the pin lets go, the pull-up takes it to the 5V pin voltage, no current (FT pin, no clamp diode)
Push-pull HIGH instead: only 3.3 V, and current flows back into the pin

tests.name: 开漏输出低：接近 0 V，从上拉灌入电流
开漏输出高：引脚松开，上拉拉到 5V 脚的电压，没有电流（FT 引脚，没有保护二极管）
换成推挽输出高：只有 3.3 V，电流倒流进引脚

compare: - 推挽高：只有 **3.31 V**，还会有 **0.29 mA** 从 5 V 经上拉倒流进引脚。5 V CMOS 输入的 VIH ≈ **3.5 V**，3.3 V 不一定能被认作高电平。
**为什么必须是 FT 引脚**：开漏“高”时引脚上是 5 V。普通引脚内部有接 3V3 的保护二极管，会把 OUT5 钳在约 3.9 V（3.3 V + 二极管压降），电流从 5 V 经上拉、二极管灌进 3V3——既输出不了 5 V，又在倒灌电源。FT 引脚没有这个二极管，可以承受 5 V。

measurements.ask: 开漏输出低：OUT5 对 GND 的电压
开漏输出低：上拉 R1 的电流（也就是引脚灌进的电流）
measurements.explain: 4.69 V / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.99 mA。上拉越小上升沿越快，但输出低时灌电流越大。

measurements.ask: 开漏输出高（引脚松开）：OUT5 对 GND
measurements.explain: 引脚不再拉，R1 里没有电流，OUT5 等于 5V 脚的 4.69 V——FT 引脚没有接 3V3 的保护二极管，所以不会被钳住。

measurements.ask: 改成推挽输出高：OUT5 对 GND
measurements.explain: 上管把 OUT5 拉在约 3.3 V，低于 5 V CMOS 的 VIH ≈ 3.5 V：不一定能被认作高电平。

measurements.ask: 同一状态：R1 的电流（从 5V 脚流向引脚）
measurements.explain: (4.69 − 3.31) / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.29 mA 从 5 V 倒流进引脚、再灌进 3V3：推挽和 5 V 上拉在打架。

hints: 起始电路：PA0 不耐 5 V。把信号线换到下排的 FT 引脚，例如 PB12。
只要一个电阻：4.7 kΩ 从 5V 脚接到信号结点。
在引脚表里选「输出 高」，并勾选「开漏」。
startNote: **找错**：5 V 上拉 R1 已经接好，但信号线接在不耐 5 V 的 **PA0** 上。**为什么**：开漏 + 5 V 上拉只能用耐 5 V（FT）的引脚。**你要做**：把信号线改接到 FT 引脚 PB12（h1），并把 PB12 设成开漏输出。
